legs.result: Started the assembled distribution with bin/solr start -Ddisable.config.edit=true -p 18983 as solrtest. The conversion warning IS written to solr.log by org.apache.solr.core.util.EnvUtils on the main thread: first log line 23:25:48.632 UTC, warning at 23:25:50.033 UTC (about 1.4s later), WebAppContext available at 23:25:50.021 UTC. The warning therefore lands at essentially the same moment the start command returns, and the BATS case asserts on the file immediately after start returns with no wait. Disclosure: the polling half of this diagnostic watched a wrong path (dist-root logs/solr.log instead of server/logs/solr.log) and is not used; the conclusion rests on the real log's own timestamps from that same start.

prior_state: Prior exact-head negative ordering proof, clean tidy and root check stand in records/receipt/shutdown-order-repack-gate-20261114.json and were not repeated, per the gate. That receipt's passed verdict covered the repack gate's stated requirements; this investigation exists because its two positive packaging runs exited 1 on the conversion case, which it disclosed.
resolution: Evidence-based resolution of the previous failure: (1) The conversion case fails identically on the unmodified contributor head on this host, so the shutdown-order branch does not cause it. (2) At a byte-identical offered tree it passed both variants on 2026-11-13 and failed both variants on 2026-11-14, and today it failed in both prescribed exact-head variants while passing in the single mutation run; the behavior is intermittent, not deterministic per head. (3) The mechanism is a startup timing race in the test on this host: the test sets -Ddisable.config.edit=true, starts Solr, and immediately asserts the conversion line is in solr.log; the diagnostic shows EnvUtils writes that line during startup at about the moment start returns, so on this slow 2-core host the assert can read the file first. (4) The added -Dsolr.pid.dir argument is not established as a cause: the contributor head fails without it. Next step for the implementation owner: treat the case as a pre-existing timing-sensitive test on this host (a wait or retry around the log assertion would close it upstream); no source change to the shutdown-order branch is indicated, and none was made.

verdict_basis: The gate's passing condition requires both prescribed full packaging commands at the exact head to exit 0; both exited 1 on the same single case. The investigation's question is answered with evidence: the failure is not a branch effect (it reproduces on the unmodified contributor head) and its mechanism is a startup timing race in the test on this host. Because the failure recurs at the exact head, the verdict is failed rather than passed; no source change was made, per the gate.
